Save and Load the Model: In this section we will look at how to persist model state with saving, loading and running model predictions.

Save and Load the Model: import torch
import torchvision.models as models
Saving and Loading Model Weights: PyTorch models store the learned parameters in an internal state dictionary, called state_dict . These can be persisted via the torch.save method:

Saving and Loading Model Weights: model = models.vgg16(weights='IMAGENET1K_V1')
torch.save(model.state_dict(), 'model_weights.pth')
Saving and Loading Model Weights: To load model weights, you need to create an instance of the same model first, and then load the parameters using load_state_dict() method.

Saving and Loading Model Weights: In the code below, we set weights_only=True to limit the functions executed during unpickling to only those necessary for loading weights. Using weights_only=True is considered a best practice when loading weights.

Saving and Loading Model Weights: model = models.vgg16() # we do not specify ``weights``, i.e. create untrained model
model.load_state_dict(torch.load('model_weights.pth', weights_only=True))
model.eval()

Saving and Loading Model Weights: Note

Saving and Loading Model Weights: be sure to call model.eval() method before inferencing to set the dropout and batch normalization layers to evaluation mode. Failing to do this will yield inconsistent inference results.

Saving and Loading Models with Shapes: When loading model weights, we needed to instantiate the model class first, because the class defines the structure of a network. We might want to save the structure of this class together with the model, in which case we can pass model (and not model.state_dict() ) to the saving function:
Saving and Loading Models with Shapes: torch.save(model, 'model.pth')
Saving and Loading Models with Shapes: We can then load the model as demonstrated below.

Saving and Loading Models with Shapes: As described in Saving and loading torch.nn.Modules , saving state_dict is considered the best practice. However, below we use weights_only=False because this involves loading the model, which is a legacy use case for torch.save .
Saving and Loading Models with Shapes: model = torch.load('model.pth', weights_only=False)
Saving and Loading Models with Shapes: Note
Saving and Loading Models with Shapes: This approach uses Python pickle module when serializing the model, thus it relies on the actual class definition to be available when loading the model.
